questions.q: What is an AWS SDK, and how does boto3 relate to the AWS CLI?
options: A language-specific library that calls the same AWS APIs as the CLI — boto3 is the official Python SDK, used constantly since most pipeline glue code is Python
The SDK is an entirely separate set of AWS services unrelated to the CLI
boto3 is a replacement for IAM that removes the need for credentials
The SDK only works for JavaScript, never Python
questions.explain: The SDK and CLI both call the same underlying AWS APIs — boto3 is just the Python-code interface to them.

questions.q: What is the difference between boto3's client and resource interfaces?
options: Client is low-level and maps almost 1:1 onto every API action for every service; resource is a higher-level, object-oriented interface available only for a subset of services
Client only works for S3, while resource works for every AWS service
They are two names for the exact same interface with no functional difference
Resource requires hardcoded access keys, while client uses the credential chain
questions.explain: Client is the universal, literal API mapping; resource is a more Pythonic layer that doesn't cover every service.

questions.q: What is the credential chain, per this lesson?
options: The fixed order of places boto3 searches for credentials automatically — environment variables, shared credentials file, and an IAM role attached to the running compute, among others
A blockchain-based system for storing AWS access keys
A single hardcoded password shared across all boto3 scripts
A manual process where a developer must always paste a key into code
questions.explain: The credential chain is how boto3 finds credentials without ever requiring a hardcoded key in the script.

questions.q: Why does code running inside a Lambda function typically never need to call boto3.client("s3", aws_access_key_id=...) with an explicit key?
options: The Lambda function's execution role provides temporary credentials automatically through the credential chain, so the SDK picks them up with zero credential handling in the code
Lambda functions are incapable of calling S3 under any circumstances
AWS disables all authentication requirements inside Lambda by default
Explicit keys are actually required and this is a trick statement
questions.explain: This is the direct payoff of the execution-role pattern from Chapter 3 — credentials flow automatically without hardcoding.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where does the SDK typically show up in a real data pipeline?
options: In Lambda functions, Glue PySpark jobs, and orchestration tasks that call AWS APIs as part of a larger program
Only in the AWS Console's search bar
Exclusively in billing and cost-management dashboards
The SDK is never used in actual pipelines, only in local testing
questions.explain: The lesson gives concrete examples: a Lambda triggered by an S3 upload, a Glue job logging via boto3, and orchestration code starting job runs.
